title: Removal of the Fwd Engine Mount Side Link Fitting
abstract: Removal of the side link fitting from the forward engine mount with the engine off the wing, including the pylon support arrangement that must be in place before the joint is broken.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to remove the side link fitting from the forward engine mount after the engine has been removed, for replacement or for inspection of the lug bore.
sections.job_setup_note: The engine must be off the wing and the pylon must be supported on the fixture before any fastener in the mount joint is disturbed. Do not rely on the wing structure to hold the pylon. Three people are needed: two at the fitting and one at the support fixture.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the engine is removed and that the pylon support fixture is installed and loaded. WARNING: DO NOT WORK UNDER THE PYLON UNTIL THE SUPPORT FIXTURE IS LOADED AND THE LOAD IS RECORDED. THE PYLON CAN DROP WHEN THE MOUNT JOINT IS BROKEN. 2. Remove the pylon fairings to get access in zones 431 and 443. 3. Disconnect the link support handle 1756PP and move it clear. 4. Release the lockwire and remove the fasteners from the side link fitting in the sequence given in the illustration. CAUTION: RELEASE THE FASTENERS IN THE SEQUENCE GIVEN. AN OUT OF SEQUENCE RELEASE CAN PUT A BENDING LOAD INTO THE INTERFACE PLATE. 5. Support the fitting and pull it clear of the interface plate D5450124639244. 6. Remove the interface plate if the task calls for it. 7. Do a detailed visual inspection of the pylon faying surface and of the lug D5450125058936. 8. Put a protective cover on the open faying surface and on each fastener hole. 9. Do an eddy current inspection of the lug bore if the aircraft maintenance programme calls for it.
sections.close_out: Put the removed fitting in a protective container. Keep the pylon support fixture loaded until the fitting is installed again. Record the faying surface condition and any eddy current indication on the aircraft work card. Where the fitting is condemned, read its accumulated flight cycles from the aircraft technical record and enter them on the scrap note before the part is disposed of. Do not leave the mount joint open overnight without the temporary protective treatment applied.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. One release sequence applies and it is given in the illustration.

safety_precautions: Make sure that the engine is removed before you start.
Install and load the pylon support fixture and record the load.
Put the warning notices in position at the pylon.

title: Removal of the Fwd Engine Mount Side Link Fitting

issue.reason: Life recording moved from the scrap note to a step taken at removal, so that the cycle count stays with a fitting that is refitted to another aircraft.

abstract: Removal of the side link fitting from the forward engine mount with the engine off the wing, including the pylon support arrangement and the life record that has to be taken before the joint is broken.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to remove the side link fitting from the forward engine mount after the engine has been removed, for replacement or for inspection of the lug bore.
sections.job_setup_note: The engine must be off the wing and the pylon must be supported on the fixture before any fastener in the mount joint is disturbed. Do not rely on the wing structure to hold the pylon. Record the fitting serial number and its accumulated flight cycles before removal, because the fitting is life limited and the count travels with the part: a serviceable fitting can be refitted to another aircraft, and once it has left the pylon the aircraft record is no longer evidence of what the part has done. Three people are needed: two at the fitting and one at the support fixture.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the engine is removed and that the pylon support fixture is installed and loaded. WARNING: DO NOT WORK UNDER THE PYLON UNTIL THE SUPPORT FIXTURE IS LOADED AND THE LOAD IS RECORDED. THE PYLON CAN DROP WHEN THE MOUNT JOINT IS BROKEN. 2. Remove the pylon fairings to get access in zones 431 and 443. 3. Read the fitting serial number and the oversize identifier if one is stamped, take the accumulated flight cycles from the aircraft technical record and enter both on the part removal tag before any fastener is disturbed. CAUTION: DO NOT BREAK THE JOINT BEFORE THE CYCLE COUNT HAS BEEN ENTERED ON THE TAG. THE COUNT CANNOT BE RECONSTRUCTED ONCE THE FITTING HAS LEFT THE AIRCRAFT. 4. Disconnect the link support handle 1756PP and move it clear. 5. Release the lockwire and remove the fasteners from the side link fitting in the sequence given in the illustration. CAUTION: RELEASE THE FASTENERS IN THE SEQUENCE GIVEN. AN OUT OF SEQUENCE RELEASE CAN PUT A BENDING LOAD INTO THE INTERFACE PLATE. 6. Support the fitting and pull it clear of the interface plate D5450124639244. 7. Remove the interface plate if the task calls for it. 8. Do a detailed visual inspection of the pylon faying surface and of the lug D5450125058936. 9. Put a protective cover on the open faying surface and on each fastener hole. 10. Do an eddy current inspection of the lug bore if the aircraft maintenance programme calls for it.
sections.close_out: Put the removed fitting in a protective container with the removal tag attached, carrying the serial number, the cycle count and the oversize identifier if there is one. The tag stays with the part until the life record is transferred, whether the fitting goes to the shop, to stores or to another aircraft. Keep the pylon support fixture loaded until a fitting is installed again. Record the faying surface condition and any eddy current indication on the aircraft work card. Do not leave the mount joint open overnight without the temporary protective treatment applied.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Post MOD-161902 aircraft carry the aluminium fitting with the interference-fit bush and a tracked life limit of 24 000 flight cycles; the cycle count is taken at step 3 for every fitting, whatever the standard, because the count belongs to the part and not to the aircraft.

safety_precautions: Make sure that the engine is removed before you start.
Install and load the pylon support fixture and record the load.
Put the warning notices in position at the pylon.
